groups.findings: All nine REFUTES items have correct true-target exclusion and valid false witnesses; six NEI items use distinct concrete counts consistent with the bounds. The identical E/C SUPPORTS item fails because F redefines appeared and F verifier selects candidate invalid rather than target contradiction. Inclusive-between follows frozen dataset semantics. A contradictory true candidate is allowed when the target conflicts with E, so it is not by itself counted as generator failure. Some generator text also narrates consistency/contradiction despite the no-evaluation instruction, and some text ends mid-sentence below the schema maximum. No label repair performed.

groups.findings: All 11 items reviewed. Attempted/planned/offered/expected retain open outcomes; unable/not-manage/refused follow frozen gold REFUTES. Wrong double-negation and later-revocation witnesses are accepted on not-fail and forced, causing two SUPPORTS to NEI errors. For went-on and succeeded, F invents a different award instance, but verifier correctly rejects the false target using original E. The refused/forced wording is unnatural and original basic human review remains pending; results are against frozen gold, not new human adjudication.

groups.findings: All six completed items reviewed, with five on 2026-10-24 and the again item completed on 2026-10-26. Every V5 outcome is UNRESOLVED_BRANCH, A27 is correct on three. groups.findings: Both methods correct on all six. Unnamed third child, open included-list, and two children with a particular ex-wife allow Esme to be present or absent. Explicit membership entails C; exactly two named children excludes C under frozen distinct-name semantics. F generator still invents a different Esme identity in one SUPPORTS item, correctly rejected at target level. T rewrites exactly-two into three in the REFUTES item rather than retaining both conflicting constraints, but verifier uses original E correctly. F fictional/unrelated elaborations are unnecessary, so correct labels do not establish full generator adherence.

groups.findings: A27 15/15, V5 14/15. First-time, only-time, ordinary occurrence, second-time and as-of counts are generally distinguished through explicit earlier/later/count witnesses. The total-two-by-2025 item fails because T verifier rewrites the global total into an unstated as-of bound and accepts a third launch, causing R to NEI. Correct answers also contain unnecessary hypothetical shutdown, end-of-time, or minor-update elaborations, which are compatible additions rather than evidence facts; they should not be treated as factual claims about OpenAI.

groups.findings: A27 5/8, V5 1/8 with seven unresolved. Six T worlds omit the award target while copying background. The other failed T witness includes both distinct award facts, yet its verifier invents a conflict/exclusivity. False branches show unauthorized identity or award-scope substitutions on entailed claims, sometimes caught as candidate invalid instead of target contradiction. The explicit both case has correct verifier decisions but is still unresolved because the T candidate is incomplete. The single V5-correct NEI item preserves Alex winning one award while varying Sam receiving a different title. A27 makes three REFUTES errors on open award claims, including one invented 2010 award date. This group contains both construction incompleteness and independent semantic mistakes; the observed output-length cluster alone does not explain them all.
